key_insight: The paper argues that anomaly and feature selection should be optimized jointly under fixed budgets, and shows a constraint-preserving XY-QAOA variant can do this more efficiently than sequential feature-first selection.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware workflows, the grouped-angle XY-QAOA design reduces circuit cost and preserves feasibility better, making larger constrained bipartite-selection problems more practical on current devices.
method: Formulate anomaly-sample and feature selection as a single joint constrained optimization problem.
Introduce Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA with grouped angles and a constraint-preserving XY mixer.
Use hardware-aware compilation and warm-start/repair strategies to improve feasible solution quality on IBM Heron R3 benchmarks.
evidence_signal: Across 36-64 qubit matched benchmarks, the implementation cut depth by 45.9%-61.3% and two-qubit gates by 2.6%-5.2%, enabled 64-qubit p=2 and 36-qubit p=3 executions, and improved feasible-sample energy quality versus random-feasible baselines.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific and still depend on feasible-sector retention, so performance may degrade as noise, calibration drift, or problem structure changes.
paper_title: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA for Joint Anomaly-Feature Selection
